challenges.says: The first criterion says more than businessrule-34650805596483639458, which only sets the destination to the Windows policy definitions folder and reports no new folder to the caller; it invents 'shows that Microsoft's package will be kept as the program's definitions' and an agreement step, and the story's 'names where the definitions go' contradicts its second criterion, where there is no folder to choose.

The third criterion drops from businessrule-24154317128059319852 that the missing English folder stops the download only after the destination files were already replaced, and the second criterion says 'nothing is stored' on extraction failure while omitting that the package file is kept and, on success, deleted (businessrule-91358402464075338920).

The second criterion promises that unpacking makes the files ready to store, citing no decision, although integrations.decision-8 and base.decision-9 assume an in-memory archive and the story's own open question admits the Windows installer package cannot be opened that way; the fact cannot carry the claim, and the criteria use 'service' wording a product owner has no use for.

The criteria on remembering a policy-source choice, falling back from an unusable policy-source place, the raw POL editing warning and creating a missing policy file cite transitions that this story's action (the Acquire ADMX Files menu item) never performs, so they say things unrelated to the story's what and why and bury unrelated behaviour in it.

The fallback criterion merges four transitions from different places (startup clearing, default templates folder, and chosen folder at Main.vb 517 which is not part of this action) into one 'cannot be loaded, uses default definitions' statement that none of the cited transitions alone says.
